analysis:
Examined the three changed files. StatusCommand.swift (head lines 135-141) now derives a display-only authorization via the new displayedProviderAuthorization, which can stay visible while the lease is unexpired and a renewal is late. The removal-readiness authorization still comes from currentProviderAuthorization, and is passed as removalAuthorization to ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary. This is a presentation change in a local, read-only CLI. It prints no new secrets and performs no network or file writes. The only added disclosure is machineID, which was already printed. UnenrollCommand+KeepServing.swift (head lines 24-25) passes removalAuthorization: authorization into summary only on the error path. The removal gate at line 23 and the re-check at lines 62-64 still use removalReady(currentProviderAuthorization), so the guard that keeps a stale or revoked authorization from prompting MDM profile removal is unchanged. The new test (StatusCommandRunTests, head lines 279-305) asserts that a late renewal shows 'MDM removal needs fresh coordinator readiness' and does not offer unenroll. This matches the intent of T-053 (stale authorization surviving) and T-057.

Unverified contract: the implementations of displayedProviderAuthorization and ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary are not in the supplied evidence. Whether displayedProviderAuthorization still enforces coordinator URL binding, expiry, revocation and connection checks cannot be confirmed here. If it were looser than intended, status could overstate authorization (T-052, T-053). The display path does not gate serving or removal, so no concrete regression is evident. A reviewer should check that displayedProviderAuthorization never returns an authorization past expiresAt, for a different coordinator, or after revocation or disconnect, and that no other caller uses it as a gate.
